correctness.rationale: From x3'=0 get x3=−x1; x1'=0 yields x1(x2−a−1)=0. If x1=0 then E0=(0,1/b,0); otherwise x2=a+1 and r²+r=1−b(a+1)=c, giving ±r iff c>0. At E± calculate Jσ=[[1,σr,1],[-σ(2r+1),−b,0],[-1,0,−1]], determinant χ(λ)=λ³+bλ²+α λ+α with α=r(2r+1)>0. Region c>0 forces 0<b<1; Routh column [1,b,α(b−1)/b,α] has signs +,+,−,+, exactly two positive-real-part roots and one negative, none on imaginary axis. Independent SymPy determinant and high-precision benchmark roots corroborate algebra. At E0 one-sided derivatives ∂x1(−|x1|)=−1,+1 differ, disproving a classical Jacobian there. Do not extend hyperbolic-index theorem to E0 or claim global dynamics.
